_header: PLANTED SYNTHETIC — POSITIVE CONTROL — NOT A MEASUREMENT OF VLD VALUE ON REAL DECISIONS.
_stage: Stage 1: 30 template instances + 10 controls = 40 Purchasing instances
_provenance_warning: F-22 COLLISION (same as Trading): _reject_sample_provenance() raises on Provenanced(source='sample') AT SCORE TIME, and spec 1.1 requires running the real scorer to compute single_pass. Resolve before the scoring pass via a harness path that bypasses the production score-time guard, or an explicit 'synthetic_control' provenance tier admitted for offline evaluation only. Never relabel as 'real_measured' to get past it.
_constant_policy_rotation: The correct hop-1 branch is deliberately ROTATED across v1..v5 in every score_keyed template, so that a constant 'always read X first' policy cannot score high. This is the fix for the S2P/Trading finding where one branch was correct in 5 of 5 variations and a no-scorer baseline reached 100%. Report every VLD delta against the constant-policy baseline (classify_branching_kind.py prints it per template), never against chance.
_lookahead_discipline: Every branch_cue and evidence_found uses only information available at order time. No hop resolves a demand or quality question using subsequent consumption.
_deviations_from_prompt: rho=0.50 conflict (5th occurrence): the per-template v5 rule contradicts the distribution table ('exactly 5'). Kept the distribution table; v5 for score_keyed templates is the rho=0.30 confidently-wrong case.

Purchasing has 6 actions but only 5 variations per template, so quality check 8 cannot mean 'all distinct'. Applied as '>=5 distinct actions per template', which every template meets — a stronger bar than the >=4 used for SOC (4 actions) and the '==5' used for DataOps/S2P/Trading (5 actions).
Check 5 (>=2 distinct actions in alternative_branches) validated over non-flat instances only; flat controls have no branches by construction.
score_keyed share is 20/40 = 50%, i.e. 10 percentage points above the spec 1.2 floor.
_single_pass_fields: Absent by design (spec 1.1). single_pass_action / single_pass_correct / why_single_pass_fails are produced by the scoring pass, not authored here.

scenarios.description: Low stock with a calendar uplift ahead; nothing states whether the uplift is real or already covered.
scenarios.why_score_keyed: Inventory is low and the calendar shows a spike in two weeks. Whether that spike is real seasonal demand, a one-off artefact in last year's data, or irrelevant because lead time already covers it is not stated anywhere \u2014 the calendar records an expected uplift, not its reliability. The routing signal is demand_forecast read against consumption_rate: where v_0 sits between the demand_pattern and stockout_risk centroids.

hops.evidence_found: 48% uplift confirmed in each of the last three years
hops.narration: Checked the demand calendar: the uplift has repeated in each of the last three years.

hops.question: Was last year's spike the same shape?
hops.branch_cue: uplift confirmed as recurring; its magnitude and duration not yet read
hops.evidence_found: same shape, 9-day duration
hops.narration: Checked the historical spike: the same shape and a nine-day duration.

decision_tree.reasoning: A reliably recurring seasonal spike that current stock will not cover.

alternative_branches.evidence_found: supplier lead time extended to 21 days against a 14-day spike
alternative_branches.reasoning: The spike lands before standard replenishment can arrive.

alternative_branches.evidence_found: on-hand plus in-transit already covers the uplift
alternative_branches.reasoning: No action beyond the routine order is needed.

alternative_branches.evidence_found: inventory_buffer_path returns stock below the reorder point
alternative_branches.reasoning: MISLEADING: a low buffer always argues for ordering more, whatever the spike's reliability.

scenarios.description: High waste rate on an item; the waste figure does not carry its own cause.
scenarios.why_score_keyed: A 30% waste rate is identical whether the item is spoiling before it can be used (shelf-life problem: order smaller and more often) or simply being over-ordered (quantity problem: order less). The waste number does not carry its own cause. The routing signal is shelf_life read against consumption_rate \u2014 where v_0 sits between the consumption_history and demand_pattern centroids.

hops.question: Is the waste spoilage or over-ordering?
hops.branch_cue: 30% waste flagged on this item; shelf_life and consumption_rate are both mid-range and the waste figure does not distinguish spoilage from over-ordering
hops.evidence_found: 7-day life but spoilage observed at day 4
hops.narration: Checked expiry data: the stated life is seven days but spoilage begins at day four.

hops.question: Does the spoilage timing match delivery cadence?
hops.branch_cue: early spoilage confirmed; delivery cadence not yet compared
hops.evidence_found: weekly delivery against a 4-day usable window
hops.narration: Checked spoilage timing: deliveries are weekly against a four-day usable window.

decision_tree.reasoning: A shelf-life problem: smaller, more frequent orders rather than the current weekly quantity.

alternative_branches.evidence_found: consumption steady; order size is twice the usable quantity
alternative_branches.reasoning: A quantity problem, not a spoilage one.

alternative_branches.evidence_found: supplier delivering stock with 3 of 7 days already elapsed
alternative_branches.reasoning: The supplier is the cause \u2014 shelf life is being consumed before arrival.

alternative_branches.evidence_found: order_size_path returns an order well above weekly usage
alternative_branches.reasoning: MISLEADING: an oversized order always looks like the cause, whether or not the stock is spoiling early.

scenarios.description: Cheaper alternative supplier available; the quoted price carries no quality, transition or contract information.
scenarios.why_score_keyed: An alternative supplier quotes a lower unit price. Whether that is a real saving depends on quality history, transition cost and contractual lock \u2014 none of which is in the quoted price. The routing signal is cost_efficiency read against quality_score and supplier_reliability: where v_0 falls between the supplier_comparison centroids for switch_supplier and order_standard.

hops.question: Is the cheaper supplier actually cheaper in total?
hops.branch_cue: alternative supplier quotes 14% below incumbent; cost_efficiency is favourable while quality_score and supplier_reliability are mid \u2014 the quote carries no quality, transition or contract information
hops.evidence_found: alternative defect rate 0.9%, audit score 92
hops.narration: Checked quality history: the alternative's defect rate and audit score both beat the incumbent.

hops.question: Does the defect record hold at our volumes?
hops.branch_cue: favourable quality confirmed; performance at our volume not yet read
hops.evidence_found: holds across three comparable accounts
hops.narration: Checked defect rates at volume: performance holds across three comparable accounts.

decision_tree.reasoning: The alternative is cheaper and measurably better; the saving is real.

alternative_branches.evidence_found: alternative defect rate 4.8% against incumbent 1.1%
alternative_branches.reasoning: The saving is spent on rejects; stay with the incumbent.

alternative_branches.evidence_found: incumbent contract locked for two more quarters
alternative_branches.reasoning: The switch is right but not yet available.

alternative_branches.evidence_found: headline_price_path returns a 14% unit-price saving
alternative_branches.reasoning: MISLEADING: the quoted price ignores requalification, defect cost and contractual lock.
